primitive_annotations.canonical_meaning: A durable identifier of a semantic object that is independent of path, blob digest and title, minted selectively, and whose continuity across carrier change is governed by explicit identity transitions.

seams.meaning_statement: Authority receipts name governing semantic IDs; AO reconstruction and knowledge must resolve the same object regardless of carrier location.
Admission binds exact subject revisions and claim identities, not governing semantic identity; covered by exact_subject_revision_binding.
AO routing and resume must reference the same workstream identity the workstream model owns (semantic_id, resume_target).
Collaboration threads use domain-local keys (MC-nnnn); AO consumes them without needing governed identity-transition semantics.
Successor bridging and migration must resolve predecessor/successor identities consistently with AO authority resolution; identity transitions are the handoff contract.
Engineering-executed carrier moves must preserve semantic identity and inbound reference resolution (path != identity).
source_refs: docs/research/258_mc0025_r8a_adversarial_reconciliation_and_amended_exact_target_candidate.md::12. Additional migration guard accepted from the review

seams.meaning_statement: Navigation and retrieval must address semantic objects rather than paths so moves do not break routes; the identity index is a shared derived view.
Evidence binds to subject digests and claim IDs; no governed semantic identity agreement is required at this seam.
An EvolutionCase binds evidence to the exact affected accepted contract identity; evolution and lifecycle must agree which object is being amended or superseded.

primitive_annotations.canonical_meaning: Binding of a receipt, decision, view or evidence record to exact content: repository identity, source path at a commit, hash algorithm, hash basis GIT_BLOB_BYTES_AT_COMMIT and content digest (or ordered input digests for same-commit views).

seams.meaning_statement: AuthorityReceipts must record exact source revisions of governing sources; AO must consume the same bytes knowledge validated.
WARRANT-F admits only for the exact subject/revision AO presents; both must bind the same subject identity and hash basis.
Workstream updates use expected-revision preconditions; continuation must fail on stale revisions.
Collaboration reviews are bound to frozen base commits; AO routing and the collaboration record must agree on which exact revision a review covers.
Bridge re-planning on staleness and migration parity evidence both require exact revision binding of current authority.
Engineering executes transitions against the exact admitted subject; the delivered subject must equal the qualified subject.
source_refs: docs/research/276_owner_total_architecture_freedom_and_warrant_f_v02_reconciliation.md::5. Generalize branch role into accepted-state subject role

seams.meaning_statement: Derived navigation/views bind ordered input digests and hash basis to prove freshness without self-reference.
Evidence records and delivered artifacts must bind the same subject digests for decision evidence to be admissible.
Evolution binds trigger evidence to the exact accepted contract revision; historical acceptance integrity depends on revision binding.

primitive_annotations.canonical_meaning: Typed derivation lineage of a fact or record: which governing sources, evidence, decisions or captures it derives from, and whether a fact is authority-sourced or successor/derived-sourced. Distinct from executor/build producer provenance, which remains assurance-domain.

seams.meaning_statement: Reconstruction and authority closure must preserve the lineage of governing facts through synthesis so that derived summaries do not become authority (KA-I07).
Admission needs evidence freshness/producer/trust provenance, which is assurance-internal and not the same concept as derivation lineage.
Workstream continuity relies on revision binding and receipts, not a shared lineage contract.
Interaction-session provenance is collaboration-domain metadata; AO does not need a shared lineage meaning here.
No authority laundering requires distinguishing authority-sourced facts from successor-derived control output across the bridge.
Engineering-executed migration must preserve provenance of each migrated unit so transition management can prove parity and rollback.
Navigation may display lineage but does not require agreement on its meaning for correctness.
Build/executor producer provenance at this seam is assurance/delivery-owned (trust, attestation), not derivation lineage.
Evolution must record what evidence triggered a change and what was superseded, and lifecycle must retain that lineage without rewriting history.

primitive_annotations.canonical_meaning: A reference to a governing object's governing status (proposed, in force, effect withheld, superseded, retired, rejected) resolved at an explicit effective/authority boundary, independent of the carrier's self-declared status text and of commit recency.

seams.meaning_statement: The authority resolver must not use latest-commit recency; it must consume explicit lifecycle and supersession semantics to decide what governs.
Admission evaluates the effective policy; weakening changes do not take effect until a governed decision, so AO decision events and WARRANT-F must agree which policy state is in force.
Workstream states (ACTIVE/PAUSED/...) are domain-owned control states, not governing lifecycle.
Collaboration messages select and authorize nothing; thread lifecycle is control state.
Current authority remains in force until an explicit switch; the bridge must bind whichever governing sources are currently in force.
Engineering may execute only transitions whose governing authorization is in force; held authorizations (e.g. physical migration) must block delivery.
Navigation and retrieval must keep superseded, rejected and current knowledge distinguishable and must not present superseded material as current.
source_refs: docs/PRINCIPLES.md::P-003. Historical material is provenance, not automatic authority

seams.meaning_statement: Evidence delivery does not carry governing lifecycle.
AO-4 dispositions (AMEND/SUPERSEDE/REOPEN) change governing lifecycle prospectively while preserving historical acceptance.

primitive_annotations.canonical_meaning: A reference to an accepted normative obligation (unit) created by a governing acceptance, together with its realization path or governed deferral. Distinct from collaboration 'obligations' (next-actor duties in a thread), which are a homonym.

seams.meaning_statement: Accepted governing obligations must activate in AO control screening from governing knowledge; both must identify the same obligation.
Verifiable obligations are realized through gates/evidence; WARRANT-F qualification and AO must reference the same obligation to close it.
Workstream pause/return conditions are workstream-owned; no shared obligation semantics required.
Collaboration 'obligations' (pending actor duties) are a different concept sharing the word; no agreement on KA-R52 meaning is required.
Migration and oracle-retirement conditions are realization paths for accepted obligations; transition management must reference the obligation it discharges.
Engineering implementation realizes accepted obligations; unrealized obligations (e.g. required production responsibilities) must remain traceable to their realization boundary.
Navigation need not agree on obligation semantics.
Evidence closure of obligations is mediated at S2; no separate shared meaning at the delivery seam.
An accepted AMEND/SUPERSEDE creates realization obligations that must be tracked rather than ending as prose.

primitive_annotations.canonical_meaning: A typed relation from a finite governed registry (e.g. REPLACE, SUPPLEMENT, SPECIALIZE, CORRECT) authored once by the natural owner end, with explicit target and scope, whose reverse edges and closure are derived.

seams.meaning_statement: Authority resolution combines governing sources by relation mode; knowledge authoring and AO resolution must interpret REPLACE/SUPPLEMENT/SPECIALIZE/CORRECT identically.
Admission does not consume governing relations.
Workstream depends_on/parent edges are workstream-domain graph relations.
No shared relation semantics required.
Successor contracts replace predecessors at governed boundaries; the bridge and transition management must agree on replacement scope.
Engineering moves carriers but does not interpret governing relation semantics; identity transitions cover its needs.
Navigation traverses derived reverse edges and closure over authored relations; navigation must not invent relation meaning.
source_refs: docs/research/217_w5_t1_v02_controlled_subject_architecture_acceptance.md::11. Structural and resolver facets remain separate

seams.meaning_statement: Not consumed at evidence delivery.
Evolution dispositions are realized as governed relations (supersession, correction, specialization) between contract versions.

negative_controls.rationale: Workstream states (ACTIVE/PAUSED/BLOCKED/COMPLETED/SUPERSEDED) are owned and defined by the workstream model; AO consumes them through one seam (S3) via that model's contract. No second domain needs to own or redefine the meaning.
DISABLED/SHADOW/ACTIVE_SUBORDINATE/SUSPENDED describe who performs control processing, explicitly separate from authority state; consumed only at the transition-management seam.
Claim/warrant internals stay inside the assurance kernel; AO consumes only the admission decision. Sharing internals would breach the accepted assurance/AO boundary.
Campaign statistics (item clusters, MDE, pairing) are assurance-internal inputs to gate outcomes such as OBSERVE_ONLY; other domains consume the gate result, not the statistic.

findings: PARTIAL_SCOPE_SUPERSESSION: DECISIONS D-011/D-015 and AO-3 as amended by its §24 are superseded only in scope. One status per unit cannot express 'superseded for scope X, in force elsewhere' without scope-qualified governed relations; a new token is not recommended.

PROPOSAL_ADOPTED_AS_AMENDED: Research 263's WMR-H V0.2 was never effective and was replaced by accepted V0.3. PROPOSED and REJECTED are both wrong; SUPERSEDED was used although its definition implies prior effectiveness. The SUPERSEDED definition should explicitly cover proposals replaced by an adopted successor, or a distinct token is needed.

STALE_SELF_DECLARED_STATUS: Research 258 and Research 276 still carry pre-acceptance status lines although their content was adopted by Research 259 and Research 311. Governing status must be resolved from lifecycle records, not carrier headers; this supports governing_lifecycle_reference as a shared primitive.

EFFECT_WITHHELD_BOUNDARY: EFFECT_WITHHELD was needed twice (Research 217 contract with W5 realization paused; AO-6 ROTATE deferred). It should mean a deliberate hold on governing effect, not merely 'accepted but not yet realized' (unrealized obligations belong to obligation/realization state), or it will absorb most accepted-but-unimplemented contracts.

RETIRED_FOR_DISCHARGED_ONE_TIME_ITEMS: RETIRED fits executed or discharged one-time governing items (D-016, Prototype V0 phase decisions, executed probe protocols, a satisfied sequencing boundary). Consider documenting 'discharged' as a RETIRED reason rather than adding a token.
TOKEN_COLLISION: EFFECT_WITHHELD avoids the HELD/SUSPENDED collisions noted in Message 003.
role_findings: CURRENT_STATE's current-stage section interleaves CONTROL and historical EVIDENCE under one heading and is the only unit flagged irreducibly multi-role.
Hand-maintained navigation and convenience indexes (KNOWLEDGE_MAP, REVIEW_INBOX) fit DERIVED semantically even though they are authored, and both contain small GOVERNING rule sections.
Workstream carriers co-locate GOVERNING definition with CONTROL state, consistent with the WMR-H definition/state split.
